fact: Statistics Botswana's Vital Statistics Report 2024 describes the Births and Deaths Registration System (BDRS) as a partially automated and decentralized system, introduced in 2003 and run through 35 district registration offices and 17 on-site registration points.
UNICEF's December 2024 report says Botswana has achieved universal birth registration.
UNICEF said under-5 birth registration in Botswana is above 90 percent, a national rate not tied to a digital system.

Statistics Botswana's Vital Statistics Report 2019 describes the Births and Deaths Registration System as computerized, networked, decentralized and real-time with a centralized database, operated by the Department of Civil and National Registration through 36 district offices and 14 onsite health-facility sites and registering 67,430 births in 2019; the system's date is given only as the 2019 reference year.

Statistics Botswana's Vital Statistics Report 2019 describes the computerized, real-time Births and Deaths Registration System as the system through which births and deaths are registered, with 13,185 current deaths registered in 2019 (80.1% completeness); the system's date is given only as the 2019 reference year.

Statistics Botswana's Vital Statistics Report 2019 estimates birth registration completeness at 100% in 2019, from registered births against census-based projected births, without tying the rate to the digital system.

The World Bank's World Development Indicators list completeness of birth registration in Botswana at 87.5%, a national rate not tied to a digital system; the line gives no year of its own, so as_of is the 2017 survey round.

The World Bank's Statistical Performance Indicators list Botswana as meeting the SDG 17.19.2 threshold of birth registration at least 90% complete and death registration at least 75% complete, a national rate not tied to a digital system; the line gives no year of its own, so as_of is the 2024 survey round.
